title: Automated Versus Manual Oxygen Titration With the EMILY.AI Device in Hospitalized Patients With Acute Respiratory Failure
official: Functional, Clinical, and Predictive Validation Study of the EMILY AI Device in Patients With Acute and Chronic Respiratory Failure: Randomized Substudy in a Conventional Hospital Ward
summary:
This randomized study evaluates EMILY.AI, an investigational (non-CE-marked) smart oxygen valve that automatically adjusts the oxygen flow delivered to a patient.

Adults admitted to the pulmonology ward of Hospital Universitario Fundación Jiménez Díaz (Madrid, Spain) with acute respiratory failure are randomly assigned to receive oxygen titrated automatically by EMILY.AI or oxygen managed as usual by the nursing team, from randomization until hospital discharge. All participants wear the device; in the usual-care group it only records data.

The study compares the time patients stay within their target saturation range, episodes of low and high oxygen, nursing workload, oxygen use, length of stay and patient experience. This substudy is part of clinical investigation FJD-EMILY-23-02, whose other substudies are registered in separate records.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Men and women aged 18 years or older.
* Admitted to the general pulmonology ward (Unit 67) of Hospital Universitario Fundación Jiménez Díaz.
* Acute respiratory failure, defined as baseline arterial PaO2 below 60 mmHg or the need for supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 above 90%. Patients on long-term oxygen therapy are eligible if a clinical deterioration requires a higher-than-usual oxygen flow to maintain SpO2 above 90%.
* Signed informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Anatomical abnormalities preventing correct placement of the pulse oximeter.
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding (women of childbearing potential require a negative pregnancy test at screening).
* Need for non-invasive ventilation or high-flow nasal cannula at admission.
* Palliative care or limitation of therapeutic effort at admission.
* Expected hospital stay under 48 hours.
* Clinical situations expected to determine length of stay independently of oxygen therapy, such as intravenous antibiotics for more than 10 days, scheduled interventional or surgical procedures, active social care needs that may delay discharge, a non-respiratory main admission diagnosis, or acute or decompensated non-respiratory comorbidities.
* Known or suspected carbon monoxide poisoning or methemoglobinemia.
* Severe hypercapnia with decompensated respiratory acidosis (pH below 7.30), hemodynamic instability requiring vasoactive drugs, or severe sepsis at admission.
* Cognitive impairment, behavioral disorder or any circumstance preventing proper use of the device or compliance with study procedures.
* Simultaneous participation in another interventional clinical trial, or readmission of a patient previously included in this study.
